evidence: qfo_graph_stage_readback_20261013.json: final profile graph refinement separates 3180 cross-species VGNC pairs later missed, 3059 with native profile-expanded edges; 3179 remain separated after satellite construction. Nineteen eventual TP rows also separate at refinement, showing that downstream rescue is not a simple monotonic effect.
hypothesis: Retaining bounded copy-rich graph families for explicit duplication-aware tree reconciliation can recover orthologs lost to pre-phylogeny singletonization or copy-component splitting without the regressions from globally broader CPM clustering.
mechanism: Add an opt-in phylogeny_deferred refinement preset. Defer existing large-copy and medium-panel-copy split rules only for families of at most 500 genes; retain all original merge rules, graph edges, HMM/profile evidence, larger-family split safeguards, satellite constraints and downstream duplication/pair rules. Default preset remains unchanged.

fixed_parameters.search: Retain admitted HMM-derived search and profile-expanded native graph for the initial mechanistic screen; no inference labels used in candidate construction.
fixed_parameters.clustering: Existing Leiden CPM 0.1 graph/partition; no resolution change.
fixed_parameters.candidate_expansion: satellite_v2 with unchanged support thresholds and high_confidence_pair retention.

stages: Regenerate default final refinement and satellite candidates from admitted native graph/partition inputs. Require exact baseline partitions and compatible constraints before evaluating the variant.

Reconcile both candidate sets with the same frozen baseline species tree as a mechanism-specific QfO diagnostic. Reproduce native control products and all deterministic control scores, preserving FAS stochastic variation.

Evaluate the variant with its independently inferred species tree and matched controls across OrthoBench, corrected QfO, and supplementary Three Kingdoms before considering promotion. Reuse compatible native gene-tree checkpoints with explicit reuse counts and checksum validation.
If the screen fails, retain all failures and scores; do not expand the deferral ceiling or choose a subset of reference families to conceal regressions.

evaluation.selection: Compare per-endpoint changes and Pareto tradeoffs against matched controls and retained tool comparators. A decline greater than 0.005 is a development screening failure, not a statistical equivalence claim. Functional similarity is not orthology proof.

implementation_gates: Experimental native CLI use requires high_sensitivity, phylogeny reconcile, satellite_v2 candidates, species_overlap rooting and positive_paralogy pair inference.

Defaults and default output semantics are unchanged. Validate bounded deferral, gene-universe preservation, deterministic ordering, boundary sizes, invalid values, CLI/API context guards, and benchmark-wrapper forwarding.
Commit and push plan and tested implementation before inference; freeze sources and all input/runtime identities in a new execution namespace.
limitations: This development hypothesis is motivated by exposed VGNC data; it does not establish universal improvement.
Graph-stage separation does not prove biological correctness of restoring every affected family.
The 500-gene ceiling is a prespecified computational safeguard, not a fitted accuracy optimum.
Larger families and unrelated split/merge behavior retain baseline policy.
The fixed-tree screen is not the final full inferred-tree pipeline or fresh full-search timing.
Existing full-search cap and held-tree experiments must finish without duplicate submissions; this mechanism uses different cached native graph inputs.
